title: Telegraph
subtitle: Build a readable telegraph with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: A telegraph communicates an upcoming attack’s timing.
overview: A telegraph communicates an upcoming attack’s timing, origin, direction, and footprint early enough for a meaningful response.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a telegraph as one rule.

demo.title: Test the telegraph
phaseDescriptions: Coordinate pose, motion, sound, effects, and arena markers so at least two channels identify the same future event without visual clutter.
The player should be able to convert the cue into a specific action—move, wait, interrupt, guard, or prepare—before commitment removes that choice.
The damaging action resolves in exactly the promised shape, then a clear cooldown separates its result from the next warning.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Coordinate pose, motion, sound, effects, and arena markers so at least two channels identify the same future event without visual clutter.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: The player should be able to convert the cue into a specific action—move, wait, interrupt, guard, or prepare—before commitment removes that choice.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: The damaging action resolves in exactly the promised shape, then a clear cooldown separates its result from the next warning.

mistakes.title: A long animation is not a useful telegraph if it does not reveal what space becomes dangerous or when commitment occurs
mistakes.body: A long animation is not a useful telegraph if it does not reveal what space becomes dangerous or when commitment occurs.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible telegraph cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune recognition time separately from movement time, then test cue visibility at combat distance, under effects, and with reduced audio or color perception.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Shorten or partially share tells only after the base vocabulary is established, preserving one reliable discriminator for each outcome.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: The damaging action resolves in exactly the promised shape, then a clear cooldown separates its result from the next warning.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A telegraph communicates an upcoming attack’s timing, origin, direction, and footprint early enough for a meaningful response. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: The player should be able to convert the cue into a specific action—move, wait, interrupt, guard, or prepare—before commitment removes that choice. Tune recognition time separately from movement time, then test cue visibility at combat distance, under effects, and with reduced audio or color perception.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: A long animation is not a useful telegraph if it does not reveal what space becomes dangerous or when commitment occurs. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
State changes are shown clearly enough to tell when the objective has advanced.
Preparation, action, and recovery create a legible cycle of pressure and release.
The mechanic earns its place by preparing, combining, or resolving nearby decisions.
